result.title: AtariBench: Evaluating Spatiotemporal Reasoning of Vision-Language Models in Atari Gameplay
result.comment: 26 pages, 14 figures. Accepted to NeurIPS 2026, Evaluations and Datasets Track
result.summary: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) have achieved strong performance on static visual understanding benchmarks, yet their ability to act in dynamic environments remains less well understood. We introduce AtariBench, a controlled benchmark that evaluates VLMs across 20 Atari 2600 games, requiring models to make sequential decisions from high-temporal-resolution gameplay streams. By decoupling fast in-game dynamics from wall-clock inference speed, AtariBench focuses on whether models can perceive rapid visual state changes, reason over spatiotemporal dynamics, and ground actions in the current observation. Our experiments reveal substantial limitations in state-of-the-art VLMs: models often fail to infer object motion and direction, exhibit brittle sequential decision-making, and over-rely on textual interaction history despite newly appended visual feedback. We further introduce a separability analysis to identify which in-game scores provide reliable signals of model competence, and use the benchmark to study how memory design and prompting strategies affect performance. Overall, AtariBench exposes a persistent gap between passive visual perception and active decision-making, providing a lightweight and rigorous testbed for developing VLMs that can reason and act in dynamic environments.

AI.brief_summary: 构建 AtariBench，用 20 款 Atari 2600 游戏的高时序分辨率画面流评测 VLM 的时空推理与序贯决策，并把游戏内动态与推理墙钟速度解耦，报告模型在物体运动方向推断、决策稳定性和依赖文本交互历史方面的缺陷，另提出可分离性分析以筛选可靠分数信号。
AI.relevance_reason: 该基准直接诊断模型是否保留并实际使用快速变化的视觉状态证据（表现为过度依赖文本历史，类似视觉旁路），可作为 LVR 中状态更新、证据获取与「看/停」决策收益评估的参考测试床。
